review_basis:
A genuinely fresh real project (Idaho Transportation Department District 2, Laboratory Heating Upgrades), pulled from the corpus_2 GitHub Release during a sixth batch-survey pass. This sheet's own PDF carries no extractable sheet-number text anywhere (title block fields read blank, top note blocks carry only keyed-notes text) -- `sheet_number` is honestly recorded as `null` rather than guessed, the only golden this session without one.

This sheet's own boiler-plant piping schematic uses a real, previously-unhandled grammar convention: a trailing `(E)` existing-marker printed AFTER the whole label (`4"CHWS(E)`, `3" HWR(E)`, `2 1/2"HWS(E)`, etc.) -- 20 real instances on this one sheet. Confirmed via direct `parseSize` testing that this format failed to parse AT ALL before a fix (`null` on every sample). This is structurally different from the already-declined LEADING `(E)` prefix convention (West Valley College's own `(E) 6"ø`, which precedes the whole label and would need a bigger grammar restructuring) -- a TRAILING marker is narrow to fix: `normalizeLabelText` in `sizes.ts` now strips `\s*\(E\)\s*$` as an early step, before anything else needs to parse past it. Fixed, tested (six new assertions in `sizes.test.ts`, 53->54), and confirmed to cause zero regressions across the full corpus (`bench:linear`'s own aggregate numbers are bit-identical before and after the fix, since no existing golden used this format).

With the fix in place, a grid sweep of fourteen of this sheet's newly-parseable labels found a real, clean 12.75 LF straight `3" HWR` (heating hot water return) pipe: `size:{kind:pipe,nps_in:3}`, `systems:["HWR"]`, confidence 0. A marked crop confirms it visually and unambiguously: the '3" HWR(E)' label's own leader points directly at this real horizontal pipe (a separate, parallel '3" HWS(E)'-labeled pipe runs just below it in the same crop, confirming this is not a mislabeled duplicate), from a real valve/union assembly near two boilers (B-1, B-2) to a real branch point feeding `2 1/2"HWR(E)`/`2 1/2"HWS(E)` continuations. `resolveRunSegments` reproduces the identical single segment and a reseed `trace_run` using the exact `bench:linear`-style seed (`seedOnLongestSegment`, standard practice since Run 95) against the freshly re-loaded, already-committed raw PDF reproduces identical points, length, size, and system exactly.

One other candidate on this same sheet (a `1 1/4"` pipe found via an `HWR(E)`-labeled seed) was swept and declined: its own automatic bind read back `systems:["HWS"]`, a real system mismatch against the label used to find it -- likely a twin-pipe crosstalk instance similar to several already-catalogued this session, not authored.
scope: A single real 3-inch heating-hot-water-return (HWR) pipe segment (12.75 LF) on the ITD District 2 Laboratory Heating Upgrades project's own boiler-plant piping schematic (unnumbered sheet, page 3), from a real valve/union assembly near two boilers to a real branch point feeding smaller continuations. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the pipe's own continuation past either boundary; the parallel `3" HWS(E)` pipe running just below it in the same crop; the declined `1 1/4"` system-crosstalk candidate noted in review_basis; every other one of the 20 real trailing-`(E)`-suffixed labels on this same sheet, not attempted this pass; every other sheet on this real 9-sheet plan set.
